english.title: Stalking involving fear of violence
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) pursued a course of conduct, namely **(..SPECIFY THE COURSE OF CONDUCT..), which amounted to stalking causing **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..) to fear, on at least two occasions, that violence would be used against

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

when you knew or ought to have known that your course of conduct would cause such alarm or distress on each of those occasions
english.legislation: Contrary to section 4A(1)(a)(b)(i) and (5) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The maximum penalty on indictment was increased from five to ten years from 3rd April 2017, this wording also applies where the conduct occurred over two or more days before and after that date, see section 175 of the Policing and Crime Act 2017. See H10642/PH97007 for offences committed before that date.
(ii) Section 4A of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 was inserted by section 111 of the Protection of Freedoms Act 2012 with effect from 25/11/2012.
(iii) See section 4A(7) the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 for an alternative verdict.
(iv) Incidents in cases of harassment must be so connected in type and in context as to justify the conclusion that they amounted to a course of conduct. See R v Patel [2004] EWCA Crim 3284
(v) Section 4A(2) and (3) regarding knowledge that a person's course of conduct will cause fear/alarm/distress.(iv) Section 4A(4) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 provides a defence.
(v) For the racially / religiously aggravated version of this offence, see document H22541.
(vi) See section 4B of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 regarding the committing of this offence by a UK national or a person habitually resident in England and Wales whilst wholly or partly in a country outside the UK.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 4A(5)(b) and (6) of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
